title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous page). Σ is a (profinite) group with a normal subgroup π and quotient G = Σ/π. Plausibly Σ is the arithmetic fundamental group of a punctured curve, π the geometric fundamental group and G a Galois group. T is a group with an action of G through a character χ (plausibly T ≅ Ẑ(1) and χ the cyclotomic character). 𝒯 is a Σ-set and J = 𝒯/π, on which G acts. Plausibly 𝒯 is the set of cusps of the universal cover and J the set of cusps of the curve.

Previous page. Grothendieck forms the discrete groupoid ⟨T,J⟩: objects J, Aut(J) = T, no maps between distinct objects. He wants a G-equivariant morphism ⟨T,J⟩ → Π^, where Π^ is the groupoid of universal coverings, identified with the groupoid of π-torsors.

Top of this page. The top part is crossed out by two long diagonal strokes, i.e. an abandoned first attempt. For J ∈ J, the π-torsor P_J maps π-equivariantly to 𝒯_J, the fibre of J under 𝒯 → J. The fibre of P_J over t ∈ 𝒯_J is a torsor under the stabiliser π_t. One considers φ(t): T → π with image in π_t.

New formulation. Restrict the Σ-action on 𝒯 to π and form the action (transport) groupoid ⟨𝒯,π⟩:
- objects: 𝒯;
- Isom(t,t') = π_{t→t'} = {λ ∈ π | λt = t'}.
Then π_0⟨𝒯,π⟩ = 𝒯/π = J and π_1(⟨𝒯,π⟩, t) = π_t. One finds that π_t centralises φ(t)(T) ⊂ π.

Hypothesis. T is commutative and φ_t: T → π_t is an isomorphism for every t. Each stabiliser (an inertia group at a cusp) is thus abelian and canonically identified with T.

Next page. This makes ⟨𝒯,π⟩ a 'T-groupoid': a not necessarily connected groupoid whose vertex groups are abelian and all identified with T, i.e. a groupoid banded by T. Σ acts on it, acting on T through G via χ.

Purpose. This is the group-theoretic/combinatorial encoding of a punctured curve's fundamental group with its cuspidal (inertia) structure. It records the cusps, their inertia subgroups, the identification of each inertia group with Ẑ(1), and Galois-equivariance. It is the 'groupe à lacets' / peripheral-structure datum needed for the paradigm/Teichmüller-tower program.
errors: The claim that π_t centralises φ(t)(T) is not automatic. It holds if φ(t)(T) ⊂ π_t and π_t is abelian, or if φ(t) lands in the centre of π_t. Grothendieck immediately adds the hypothesis φ_t: T ≅ π_t with T commutative, which makes it trivial. So it is a gap patched by an assumption rather than an error.
The first part of the page (down to roughly 'dans π_t centralise') is struck through by two diagonal lines, so it is a discarded attempt. The machine transcription does not mark this.

ideas.what: Action groupoid ⟨𝒯,π⟩ of a π-set, with π_0 = orbit set and π_1 = stabilisers
ideas.where_published: groupoid viewpoint pervasive in SGA1 and Esquisse; not this exact notation

ideas.what: Discrete groupoid ⟨T,J⟩ with every vertex group T, mapped equivariantly into the groupoid of π-torsors (universal covers)
ideas.modern_name: family of base points / cusps as a functor into the fundamental groupoid; 'packets' of tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Grothendieck, Esquisse 1984 (fundamental groupoids with many base points)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (fundamental groupoids based at sets of base points), in spirit

ideas.what: T-groupoid: groupoid whose vertex groups are abelian and coherently identified with a fixed T, with Σ acting compatibly via the character χ on T (inertia groups at cusps identified with Ẑ(1))
ideas.modern_name: banded groupoid / T-gerbe-like datum; cuspidal inertia structure, peripheral structure, 'synchronization of cyclotomes'
ideas.usually_credited_to: Esquisse's 'groupes à lacets' (Grothendieck); later Nakamura, Mochizuki (cuspidal inertia, cyclotomic synchronization, 1990s–2000s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions profinite groups 'à lacets' (discrete structure of loops); the explicit groupoid formalism is not in published texts as far as I know

missed.claim: The cuspidal structure of π_1 of a punctured curve is packaged as a Σ-equivariant groupoid banded by T = Ẑ(1). The inertia groups at all cusps are identified with a single T compatibly with the Galois action through χ. This anticipates the later anabelian notion of synchronising the cyclotomes of the inertia groups (Mochizuki) and gerbe-theoretic formulations of cuspidal data, but phrased as a T-groupoid.
missed.quote: supposons T commutatif et φ_t : T ⥲ π_t
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean categorical (banded-groupoid) formulation of 'groupes à lacets' that is apparently unrecorded. That could be useful for the combinatorial anabelian geometry of Grothendieck–Teichmüller towers, but it is mostly a reformulation.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is elementary groupoid bookkeeping. The interest is that it shows Grothendieck's precise formalism for cusps and inertia ('lacets') in the paradigm notes as Galois-equivariant T-banded groupoids, which foreshadows later anabelian cyclotome-synchronization ideas. The underlying concepts are known, though, and the page is partly abandoned.
transcription_corrections: The top block of the page (about lines 1–8) is struck through by two diagonal lines; the transcription should mark it as deleted.
'Considérons la restriction de l'opération de ℰ sur 𝒯 : π' should read 'Considérons la restriction de l'opération de Σ sur 𝒯 à π', hence the groupoid ⟨𝒯,π⟩.
'⟨^τ𝒯, π⟩' should be ⟨𝒯, π⟩; the 'τ' prefixes on J and 𝒯 are artefacts of Grothendieck's handwriting of script letters.
'J ∈ ^τJ' should read 'J ∈ J' (the script J of the orbit set).
'= fibre de J de 𝒯_π dans 𝒯' should read 'fibre de J (de 𝒯 → 𝒯/π) dans 𝒯'.
The last line likely begins 'en plus de 𝒯 Σ-ensemble, ...'; the remainder is illegible.
